speaker: facilitator
text: Design session started. Question: Propose 3 items to improve the tool

speaker: claude
text:
The proposal is three fixes, each tied to a specific defect I read in the code: a new run can wipe an existing session, long debates are summarised from a trimmed transcript, and nothing checks the `verified (path:line)` citations.

**1. Refuse to overwrite an existing log.**
Without `--resume`, the runner writes an empty file over `NAME.jsonl` — verified (agent-design-session.ts:780-781). Nothing checks first whether the file exists: there is no `stat`, `access` or `exists` call — verified (grep over agent-design-session.ts). The launcher makes this easy to hit. Its output name defaults to `${question%.*}-session` — verified (agent-design-session.sh:59). So running `./agent-design-session.sh my-question.md` a second time without `--resume` wipes the first session.
- **Fix:** if `NAME.jsonl` is not empty, stop with a message pointing to `--resume` or a new `--out`. Add `--force` for anyone who really wants to overwrite.
- **Risk:** it breaks scripts that rely on overwriting silently. I accept that.

**2. Trim on entry boundaries, and keep the opening proposal and notes.**
- `transcriptForPrompt` keeps only the last 28,000 characters, cut at a raw character position — verified (:21, :301-303). The first entry the agents see can start mid-sentence.
- Only answers and their decision records are pinned — verified (:280-293). The README admits notes can drop out (README.md:57-58).
- The decision record is written from the same trimmed text — verified (:871). In a long session, whoever writes the record may never see the round-1 proposal it is judging.
- How many rounds it takes to pass 28k is unverified. At about 400 words per turn I estimate roughly 5-6 rounds, but turn length is not enforced.
- **Fix:** drop whole entries from the front instead of cutting characters. Always keep the designer's first turn and every `note`. Give the decision-record prompt a larger budget.
- **Risk:** prompts get bigger. `--context-file` already has no size cap (smoke test at test/smoke.sh:81-86), so this cap protects little.

**3. Check citations mechanically after each turn.**
The tool's main promise is `verified (path:line)` (README.md:108-111; the rule itself is at :344-345), but the runner never checks a citation.
- **Fix:** after `record(...)` at :838, parse the markers. Flag any citation whose file is missing under `repo` or whose line number is past the end of the file. Add the warning as a facilitator line in the transcript so the reviewer sees it. This needs no model calls.
- **Risk 1:** false alarms on line ranges (`:280-293`), short forms like `(:871)`, or paths outside `--repo`. The parser has to accept those forms.
- **Risk 2:** the check proves only that a citation points at a real line, not that the line supports the claim. It must be labelled "citation resolves", never "verified".

**Considered and left out:**
- **`--repo` is not saved in `Meta`** — verified (:213, :719). Resuming from another directory points the agents at the wrong tree. It is real but already documented (README.md:97), so it ranks below item 3.
- **No timeout on agent calls** — verified (:36-66). Also, the temporary scratch directory is deleted only when `main` finishes normally — verified (:899, :902-906). A hung CLI stops the whole session. That is worth fixing, but it hurts less than losing a session (item 1) or a misleading decision record (item 2).

**Assumption:** most users run sessions through the shell launcher with its default output name. That is unverified; if it is wrong, item 1 matters less.

speaker: codex
text:
I would keep session protection and context repair, but replace citation checking with recovery from damaged logs.

1. **Prevent accidental replacement atomically.** The non-resume branch empties the JSONL file before recording metadata, verified (agent-design-session.ts:780-782), and the positional launcher derives a repeatable output name, verified (agent-design-session.sh:59).

   Your existence check is insufficient if two launches race. Use exclusive file creation so only one process can claim a basename; reject existing files even when empty. Also protect an existing Markdown output: recording an entry rewrites that file, verified (agent-design-session.ts:772-776). Offer explicit `--force` replacement.

   **Accepted trade-off:** scripts that intentionally reuse basenames need adjustment. Atomic creation prevents competing new sessions; preventing concurrent resumptions would require additional locking.

2. **Preserve coherent evidence within an explicit context budget.** The transcript currently slices through rendered text at a character boundary, verified (agent-design-session.ts:295-303). The decision writer receives that same trimmed transcript and is instructed to use only the supplied debate, verified (agent-design-session.ts:871; agent-design-session.ts:382-395).

   Keep whole entries, preserve moderator instructions, and report exactly which entries were omitted. Give synthesis the complete debate when it fits; otherwise require an explicit compaction step that preserves proposals, objections, corrections, and unresolved claims.

   I reject “always pin the opening proposal and increase the budget” as a complete solution: an intermediate correction can matter more than the opening position. Nor does uncapped background make another cap useless; those inputs consume the same finite model context.

   **Accepted trade-off:** compaction adds complexity and can distort meaning. Preserve original entries in the log and identify any generated summary as such.

3. **Recover valid log entries after an interrupted write.** There is a stronger durability problem than unchecked citations: `readExisting` parses every line inside one `try`, then returns an empty array on any read or parse failure, verified (agent-design-session.ts:529-535). Resume consequently reports “no previous turns” rather than distinguishing corruption from absence, verified (agent-design-session.ts:735-737).

   Parse incrementally, distinguish missing files from malformed records, and offer explicit recovery of the valid prefix when the final record is incomplete. Report interior corruption with its line number; do not silently skip it or discard the damaged bytes.

   **Assumption:** interruption can leave a partial final append; I have not reproduced this. **Accepted trade-off:** recovery needs a clear operator choice before changing the log.

Citation resolution remains useful, but it establishes addressability, not support for a claim. I prioritize preserving and recovering the evidence first. This was a read-only inspection; I ran no tests.

speaker: moderator
text: Moderator note: Since we are going to improve logging I want to persist repo option to be used when resuming

speaker: claude
text:
I'm accepting Codex's item 1 and agreeing on item 2. I'm replacing citation checking with one logging item: it tells a missing log apart from a damaged one, and it saves `--repo`, as the moderator asked.

**1. Exclusive creation: accepted, with one consequence.** The runner uses `writeFile` from `node:fs/promises` on both runtimes — verified (agent-design-session.ts:5, :27). So the fix is `writeFile(jsonl, "", { flag: "wx" })` in place of :781. Whether Deno's `node:` layer honours `wx` is unverified. I'm adopting Codex's other two points: also guard the `.md` file (rewritten at :776), and reject empty files too.

**2. Context: agreed.** Drop whole entries, report what was dropped, and give the full debate to whoever writes the decision record when it fits. I withdraw "pin the opening proposal" as the whole answer.

**3. The log becomes the place session settings are stored and recovered from.**

*Where I disagree with Codex on severity:* damage is never silently carried forward. Every caller stops when `readExisting` returns `[]` — verified (:554, :702, :737, :759). The real danger is that item 1 removes the workaround. Today a user with a truncated log can just start over. After item 1 their only options are `--force`, which throws away every valid turn, or editing the JSONL by hand. So recovery belongs in the same change as item 1:
- `readExisting` reports "missing" separately from "malformed at line N".
- If only the last line is damaged, `--resume` offers to continue from the valid lines before it, and keeps the damaged bytes in a side file.

*Persist `repo`:*
- **Storage:** add `repo` to `Meta` (:213). Store it relative to the log, the way `parent` already is (:762, :765). Resolve it the way `parentOf` does (:539-541), then call `realpath`. `relative()` was written for file targets (:264). It gives correct but longer-than-needed paths for directories — verified by reading the code, not run.
- **Order:** `realpath` currently runs at :719, before `meta` is known (:744, :761). It has to move after both branches. Move the scratch-dir creation (:723-725) after it too. Otherwise a missing saved repo leaks the temp dir, because cleanup only runs on a normal exit (:899, :902-906).
- **When `--repo` differs from the saved one:** the flag wins, as with `context` (:745), not a hard error as with `designer` (:746-748). A moved checkout is a legitimate case. Only `entries[0].meta` is ever read (:744), so on its own an override would be forgotten on the next resume. The runner therefore appends a `meta` facilitator entry: "Repository changed from X to Y; earlier citations refer to X". On resume it reads the last `meta.repo`. How `markdownDocument` and `transcriptForPrompt` treat a second `meta` entry is unverified.
- **Follow-up:** the child inherits the parent's repo, as with `designer` (:764). The parent's relative path is resolved against the parent's directory, then rewritten relative to the child's log.
- **Old logs:** if there is no `meta.repo`, fall back to the flag or the current directory.
- **Docs:** update README.md:95-97 and the `--repo` help text at :75-76 to say "Saved in the log", matching :87.

**Risks I accept:**
- Moving a log without its repo breaks the link. The error should name the saved path and suggest `--repo`.
- A saved repo only fixes the directory, not the commit. If the tree changes between runs, earlier `path:line` citations can go stale without warning. Saving the git HEAD would close that gap, but I'm leaving it out of scope.
- Committed logs will now contain relative repo paths.

**Assumption:** a truncated last line is the realistic kind of damage, not damage in the middle of the file. Like Codex, I have not reproduced it. I ran nothing; I only read the code.

speaker: codex
text:
Repository persistence belongs in item 3, but your proposed metadata update needs explicit handling for prompt visibility and decision reuse.

1. **Protect both output files.** Keep exclusive creation, but treating `writeFile(jsonl, "", { flag: "wx" })` as the entire fix leaves the Markdown collision unresolved: recording an entry rewrites that output, verified (agent-design-session.ts:772-776).

   Reserve both paths before starting; if the second reservation fails, remove only the empty file this attempt created. Keep replacement behind explicit `--force`. **Accepted trade-off:** creating two files is not one atomic operation, so interrupted reservation can leave an empty file requiring attention. Concurrent resume remains outside this protection.

2. **Budget coherent evidence.** Keep whole entries and an omission manifest, with a separate synthesis budget. The current decision writer receives the same trimmed transcript as debate turns, verified (agent-design-session.ts:836, agent-design-session.ts:871).

   Specify what happens when preserved moderator instructions and evidence alone exceed the budget: require explicit compaction or stop with an actionable message. Increasing the limit cannot define that boundary. **Accepted trade-off:** compaction can distort meaning; retain original entries and identify summaries and their source entries.

3. **Recover logs and persist the effective repository.** Your correction on corruption severity is fair: resume stops when reading returns no entries, verified (agent-design-session.ts:735-737). The defect is lost diagnostics and unavailable recovery, rather than silently continuing with damaged history.

   My concrete objection concerns the appended `meta` warning. Additional metadata entries appear in Markdown because rendering includes every entry after the first, verified (agent-design-session.ts:459-462), but **all metadata entries are excluded from debate prompts**, verified (agent-design-session.ts:295-299). Furthermore, a metadata update would not trigger a fresh decision: decision reuse checks subsequent notes, verified (agent-design-session.ts:799-803).

   Persist the repository update as structured metadata, and record a moderator note explaining the change so agents see it and synthesis is reconsidered. Fold repository updates over the initial settings; use that same resolver for resume and parent inheritance. Follow-up inheritance currently reads initial metadata directly, verified (agent-design-session.ts:761-764).

   Define precedence as explicit flag, saved repository, then current directory; for new follow-ups, substitute the parent’s effective repository. Store paths relative to their owning log and resolve before rebasing into a child.

**Assumptions and accepted risks:** repository overrides represent intentional relocation; a damaged final record is a plausible interruption case, unverified experimentally. Accept relocation failures and stale citations after tree changes. Recovery should require explicit selection, preserve damaged bytes, and refuse interior corruption.

Proposed validation: resume from another directory, override then resume again, inherit into a differently located child, and recover a truncated final record. I inspected code only; no tests or edits.

speaker: claude
text:
Codex is right that an appended `meta` entry is invisible to the agents. I'm rejecting both parts of the fix: the moderator note, and the forced new decision record. Here is a smaller change.

**1. Don't record the repo change as a moderator note.**
- Notes appear in the Markdown as "Moderator (you)" — verified (agent-design-session.ts:429-430).
- Agents are told that a `Moderator note:` line is the human's instruction — verified (:350-351).
- A note written by the tool would therefore put words in the human's mouth, and agents would follow it as an instruction.

**Fix:** keep one structured entry and make it visible.
- Only the first entry should be hidden from prompts. Today the filter at :298 drops every `meta` entry; it should drop only index 0.
- A later `meta` entry then reaches the agents as `FACILITATOR:` (:299, :270-273).
- The Markdown already titles it "Facilitator", through the default case — verified (:433-434).
- The result is one entry, no false attribution, and no new kind.

**2. A repo change should not force a new decision record.**
The decision-writer's prompt has no `repo` parameter. It gets only the topic, the pinned entries, the transcript and the context, and is told to use "only the debate below" — verified (:382-385). Writing the record again would reuse the same debate with one extra line, and still check no citations. A checkout that has only moved does not change what was argued.
- **Fix:** leave the reuse check at :801 as it is. If the tree's contents changed, the honest response is `--rounds N`: the agents then re-read the code.
- **Risk I accept:** a kept record may cite lines in a tree that has since changed. Saving the git HEAD, which I put out of scope last turn, is the real fix for that.

**3. The fold must also cover `context`, which has the same bug.**
On resume, `--context-file` overrides the saved context for that run only. It is never written back, and the next resume reads `entries[0].meta` again — verified (:744-745). The resolver Codex proposes should fold every later `meta` entry over the first, with keys limited to `repo` and `context`. `designer` stays fixed, as now (:746-748). `parent` stays fixed too: you can't add `--follow-up` on resume (:750-751).
- **Type change:** `designer` is required in `Meta` (:213). Later entries need `Partial<Pick<Meta, "repo" | "context">>`, or the fold has to reject them.
- **Follow-ups use the same resolver.** Today the inherited context and designer are read from `parentEntries[0]` (:761, :764), so a parent's override would be lost.

**Precedence:** agreed. The explicit flag wins, then the folded saved value, then the current directory. A new follow-up takes the parent's folded repo. Every stored path is relative to the log that owns it.

**Item 1:** I accept reserving both files and rolling back if the second reservation fails. The extra case is a `.md` that exists with no `.jsonl`. That should also be refused, not treated as an orphan: `--render` can rebuild the `.md` (:699-705), but nothing can rebuild a lost `.jsonl`.

**Assumptions:**
- Overrides are rare, so a second `meta` entry in the debate costs little prompt space.
- The `kindOf` fallback that turns index 0 into `meta` (:218) does not misfire on later entries, because they carry an explicit `kind`.

I only read the code; I ran nothing.

speaker: codex
text:
I withdraw the moderator-note proposal and automatic resynthesis for repository relocation, but persisting context overrides makes unchanged decision reuse incorrect.

1. **Protect both outputs.** Retain exclusive reservation of JSONL and Markdown, rollback limited to files created by that attempt, and explicit `--force`. Recording rewrites Markdown after appending JSONL, so protecting only JSONL leaves an overwrite path—verified (agent-design-session.ts:772-776).

   **Accepted trade-off:** interrupted reservation can leave an empty file; concurrent resume still requires separate locking.

2. **Preserve coherent context.** Your facilitator entry solves attribution, provided updates explicitly use `speaker: "facilitator"`: prompt labels derive from the speaker, and Markdown’s default title does too—verified (agent-design-session.ts:270-273; agent-design-session.ts:433-434).

   However, changing the metadata filter alone does not guarantee visibility. Those entries would still pass through front trimming—verified (agent-design-session.ts:295-303). Keep the update history within the entry-based budget, and supply effective repository and context settings independently of that history. Include settings and pinned material when calculating the budget.

   **Accepted trade-off:** when required material exceeds the budget, explicit compaction or an actionable stop remains necessary.

3. **Recover logs and persist effective settings, with field-specific decision reuse.** I accept your restricted fold: mutable `repo` and `context`, fixed `designer` and `parent`, shared by resume and follow-up inheritance. Today both resume and inheritance obtain saved context from initial metadata—verified (agent-design-session.ts:744-745; agent-design-session.ts:761).

   My objection is specifically to leaving the reuse check unchanged after adding persistent **context** updates. Synthesis receives context directly, separately from the debate—verified (agent-design-session.ts:382-395). Yet reuse currently checks only for subsequent notes, then bypasses synthesis when a record is retained—verified (agent-design-session.ts:799-803; agent-design-session.ts:865-871). Persisting changed context could therefore leave the displayed decision based on the previous context.

   Invalidate reuse when effective context changes. For a repository-path change alone, retain the historical decision and display the relocation warning without implying renewed verification.

   Also distinguish a successfully parsed record from a valid settings update. The reader currently casts parsed JSON to `Entry` without validating its structure—verified (agent-design-session.ts:529-532). Validate update keys and value types before folding; report malformed updates with their physical line numbers. Recover an incomplete final record only through explicit selection, preserving damaged bytes and refusing interior corruption.

**Assumptions and accepted risks:** repository overrides represent intentional relocation; partial final writes remain unverified experimentally. Context changes justify fresh synthesis, which adds a model call but does not recheck repository evidence.

Proposed checks include override-then-resume, changed context after a decision, child inheritance, and truncated-tail recovery. I inspected code only; no tests or edits.

speaker: facilitator
text:
## Decision

Adopt three improvements:

1. **Protect both session outputs.** Reserve JSONL and Markdown paths exclusively, rejecting existing files even when empty. If reservation fails, remove only empty files created by that attempt. Require explicit `--force` for replacement.
2. **Preserve coherent evidence within explicit budgets.** Trim whole entries, identify omissions, preserve moderator instructions, and count effective settings and pinned material toward the budget. Give synthesis the complete debate when it fits; otherwise require explicit compaction or stop with an actionable message. Retain originals and identify summaries and their sources.
3. **Improve log recovery and persist the repository.** Distinguish missing logs from malformed records, report physical line numbers, and offer explicitly selected recovery of an incomplete final record while preserving damaged bytes. Refuse interior corruption. Save `repo` relative to its owning log and use its effective value for resume and follow-up inheritance. Precedence is explicit flag, saved value, then current directory; new follow-ups inherit the parent’s effective repository.

Repository updates should use structured metadata with an explicit facilitator speaker, remain visible as history, and supply effective settings independently of trimming. Repository relocation alone retains the historical decision with a warning. Persistent context overrides remain a scope decision below; if included, changed effective context should invalidate decision reuse. Keep `designer` and `parent` fixed and validate settings updates before folding them.

## Rationale

These priorities protect the session and the evidence supporting its decisions. Repository persistence implements the moderator’s settled request. Separating repository relocation from context changes avoids implying renewed code verification while preventing reuse of a decision synthesized with obsolete context.

## Alternatives rejected

- Existence checks alone or protection of JSONL alone leave race or Markdown overwrite paths.
- Pinning only the opening proposal and increasing limits can still lose consequential corrections.
- Citation checking is deferred: resolving an address does not establish support for a claim.
- Tool-generated moderator notes misattribute instructions to the human.
- Automatic resynthesis for repository relocation alone provides no renewed evidence check.
- Git HEAD persistence and concurrent-resume locking remain outside this proposal.

## Risks

- Existing scripts must explicitly authorize replacement; interrupted reservation can leave empty files.
- Compaction can distort meaning.
- Moving logs can break relative repository paths; tree changes can stale citations.
- Fresh synthesis after context changes adds a model call without rechecking repository evidence.
- Recovery changes the log and therefore requires explicit operator selection.

## Claims still unverified

The debate reports code inspection only; no tests or edits were performed. Unverified assumptions include:

- Deno’s `node:` compatibility layer honors exclusive creation with `wx`.
- Interrupted writes produce incomplete final records, and tail damage is the realistic recovery case.
- Most users use launcher-derived output names; overrides are rare and represent intentional relocation.
- The 28,000-character limit is reached after roughly five or six rounds.
- Explicit kinds prevent the metadata fallback from misclassifying later entries.

The proposed reservation, recovery, metadata folding, visibility, inheritance, and decision-reuse behavior remain untested.

## Questions for the human

- **Do you want persistent context overrides included alongside the requested repository persistence?** Recommended default: **yes**, with validated updates and fresh synthesis whenever effective context changes.
- **Do you want explicit compaction implemented in this change, or should sessions stop when required material exceeds the budget?** Recommended default: **stop with an actionable message**, deferring compaction.
